      "title": "Getting Started",
      "properties": {},
      "widgets_values": [
        "# Your First Image\n\nA simple **text-to-image** workflow for local users and modest GPUs. Work through each section left to right, then click **Queue** to generate.\n\nThis starter uses **DreamShaper 8** — a **fine-tuned** checkpoint built on the original **Stable Diffusion 1.5** base (2022). It keeps SD 1.5's speed and low VRAM needs while improving overall image quality. Newer base models (Z-Image, Flux, Qwen Image, etc.) look better but need more hardware.\n\n**Steps:**\n1. Load Model\n2. Prompt\n3. Image Size\n4. Sampling\n5. Save\n\nTip: use **512×512** — the native resolution SD 1.5 was trained on."
      ],
      "color": "#222",
      "bgcolor": "#000"
    },

      "title": "Note: Load Model",
      "properties": {},
      "widgets_values": [
        "**Load Checkpoint** selects your model file (.safetensors). It outputs the **model**, **CLIP** (reads your prompt), and **VAE** (decodes the final image).\n\n**DreamShaper_8_pruned** is a **fine-tuned** version of the original **SD 1.5** base model — not the raw checkpoint itself. It was trained further on curated images to improve quality and versatility. The `_pruned` suffix means extra weights were trimmed to keep the file smaller and faster to load on modest GPUs.\n\nPut checkpoint files in `ComfyUI/models/checkpoints/`. When switching models, check its docs — each fine-tune or base model may need different resolutions, samplers, and prompt styles."
      ],
      "color": "#222",
      "bgcolor": "#000"
    },
    {
      "id": 12,
      "type": "MarkdownNote",
      "pos": [

        560

      "title": "Note: Prompt",
      "properties": {},
      "widgets_values": [
        "Describe what you want in the **positive** prompt (green). List things to avoid in the **negative** prompt (blue).\n\n**SD 1.5 prompt style:** This generation of models works best with **comma-separated tags** rather than full sentences — e.g. `masterpiece, best quality, 1girl, blonde hair, cinematic lighting`. Quality boosters and a detailed **negative** list (as shown here) are typical for SD 1.5 era models.\n\nNewer models often prefer natural-language sentences. When you switch checkpoints, check how that model expects prompts to be written.\n\nStart by editing the example text and re-running to see how changes affect the result."
      ],
      "color": "#222",
      "bgcolor": "#000"
    },

      "title": "Note: Image Size",
      "properties": {},
      "widgets_values": [
        "**Empty Latent Image** sets width, height, and batch size.\n\n**Why 512×512?** SD 1.5 was trained at **512px** — DreamShaper 8 inherits this. Staying near 512 gives the best results. Very large sizes (e.g. 1536+) often look worse, use more VRAM, and run much slower.\n\n**Other models, other sizes:** SDXL uses ~1024, Flux uses different sizes again. Always check the model card before changing width/height.\n\nStart at **512×512**. Only go larger after 512 runs smoothly, and only if your model supports it."
      ],
      "color": "#222",
      "bgcolor": "#000"
    },

      "title": "Note: Sampling",
      "properties": {},
      "widgets_values": [
        "**KSampler** generates the image.\n\n- **Steps** (20) — more detail, but slower\n- **CFG** (8) — how strongly the prompt is followed\n- **Seed** — randomize for variety; fix to repeat a result\n- **Sampler** — euler is fast and fine for starters\n\nWant more detail? Select the **KSampler** node and click **Node Info** in the toolbar — ComfyUI includes built-in docs explaining each parameter."
      ],
      "color": "#222",

      "title": "FAQ",
      "properties": {},
      "widgets_values": [
        "**Can I use this template for any model?**\n\nNo. This workflow is designed for **SD 1.5** checkpoints like DreamShaper. Other model types — SDXL, Flux, Qwen Image, video models, etc. — need different nodes, loaders, resolutions, and prompt styles. Simply swapping in a different model here usually won't work.\n\n**What should I do instead?**\n\nOpen the **template library** and find a workflow that matches your model type. Those templates come with the correct pre-built pipeline already wired up. Start from the matching template, then customize — swap models, edit prompts, and adjust settings on a working foundation."
